newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai mills seek May soymeal, corn buying heard.
newsitem.headline: Thai mills seek May soymeal, corn buying heard.

text.p: Easier prices on the US soy futures complex drew mixed reaction this week from the Thai feedmill industry as some bought while others awaited further falls, trade sources said on Tuesday.
Some modest buying of May soymeal was seen, they added.
"Total buying since last week could be around a cargo or so. Those who bought seemed to believe that the price could edge up," said one trader from a US house.

"But those who remained sidelined think prices are still too expensive and should come down further. With local output coming to the market soon, I guess they think they can afford to wait," he added.

Local soymeal was quoted slightly higher at 9.65 baht a kg ($0.37) from 9.60 baht last week. US soymeal for May/June delivery was indicated at $360 per tonne c&f Bangkok, Indian product at $338-340 and South American at $325-340, depending on grade.
There was market talk that a major mill had bought another 50,000 tonnes of corn from Argentina for March shipment. This was on the top of 50,000 tonnes ordered in December for April shipment.
"The buyer might expect that the government will have already come up with details on zero-tariff corn imports by the time the shipments arrive in May or June," said one trader.
Charoen Pokphand in December bought 50,000 tonnes of Argentine corn for April shipment at $130 per tonne c&F Si Chang, a port in eastern Chonburi province near Bangkok.

Activity in the local corn market picked up this week on improved demand, pushing prices up. Corn edged up to 4.40 baht a kg from 4.25 baht last week, trade sources said. --Bangkok newsroom (662) 652-0642
